To announce the kill

assessments.note: card contested, the bank narrowed to what is settled (ppm-159/1, u01): The printed wording asked about kill-sharing, not the card's question. Field literature (Sunquist, Wild Cats of the World; San Diego Zoo fact sheet after Schaller 1967) lists roaring after killing a large animal, "to announce a large kill", among tiger roars; the card's "to invite other tigers to share" is unsupported (tigers generally do not share). The purpose is not studied in depth, so related answers are accepted in notes.

their studies have led to the identification of nearly 300 individual tigers based on their unique stripe patterns

assessments.note: Panthera led the 2022 IUCN Red List tiger assessment.

Because cats have adapted to conserve energy via long periods of rest and sleep, it is possible that purring is a low energy mechanism that stimulates muscles and bones without a lot of energy.

assessments.note: Answer by geneticist Leslie A. Lyons (UC Davis); hypothesis, not proven — the bank's wording says 'suspect'.

support.quote: As of 2022, there were 3,682 wild tigers in India, which is almost 75% of the world's wild tiger population.
India is the country with the largest number of wild tigers Around 3,700 of the world's wild tigers are in India

assessments.note: Against the IUCN 2022 range of 3,726–5,578 (mean ~4,500), India's ~3,700 is a clear majority.

support.quote: No two tigers have the same stripe patterns, which helps us identify and monitor individual tigers over time.
based on whether the hyoid bone of the larynx is incompletely ("roarers") or completely ("purrers") ossified

assessments.note: Supports the traditional hyoid link; the paper itself argues roaring depends more on the vocal folds and long vocal tract — the wording says 'traditionally been linked'.
